text: Evening, all. Two soldiers, two nice quiet spots in my own desert. Nothing to worry about, Rich, Silke, they're just enjoying the view. As for tax, Reina, Your Majesty, the desert doesn't pay tax. The desert *is* the tax. Anyone who wants my soldiers off the board knows the price: twenty each, and I'll smile while I take it.

The heavens speak to the throne, so the throne will read them. I'll shuffle the twenty cards myself and take nothing for it; the omens aren't for sale at this table. And Rob, enjoy the view while you can. The Wall was built to watch exactly that kind of desert.

Your Majesty, what a pleasure to farm under such a steady hand, and under such a fine Wall. Silke, Paddy, the customary five each, if you'd be so kind. It's the old rate, the honest rate, and I won't ask a grain more of you this year. You have my word, and my word is the one thing I don't charge for. Rob, do enjoy the view. Just remember my granary feeds the whole table, your soldiers included.
Rich asks Silke and Paddy for the minimum rent, 5 each, and they pay it.

Forty percent, while the fields are full. A dynasty is built in the good years, not begged for in the lean ones. The Summer Palace goes up first; the Wall and the Canal come after it. Clark, five for the collecting, by the book. Rob, the desert can call itself whatever it likes, but your share is twenty-four, and I'll be counting it.
Reina declares a tax of 40%: 24 each from Clark, Rich, Silke and Paddy. Rob refused the tax at the setup (the Warlord may), so he owes none. The crown builds the Summer Palace alone, for 20.

Twenty-four from each of us, Clark included, and I'll count it out in front of everyone. Rob, your refusal goes in the ledger: Year One, Warlord declines the crown's due. Your Majesty, forty percent in the first year is bold. I'll write that down too, purely as a record of the good years, you understand.
Clark collects the tax: 24 each from Clark, Rich, Silke and Paddy, 96 to the crown.
The Summer Palace stands at G20, in the heart of the province, under the Wall and well clear of the dunes. Let the desert admire it from a distance, Rob. A respectful distance.
Reina builds the Summer Palace on G20, for 20 from the crown. 870 of the works are still owed. Now the auctions.
The Harvest Pile is the common bank: Rich keeps it and pays the harvests out of it, but its grain isn't his.

My Customs House goes up at two, honest price, and anyone who wants the crown's paperwork on their mantel is welcome to it. I'll bid modestly on the rest. I won't be the man who poured the table's grain into the Harvest Pile in Year One, and I'll remember who does.

A magnificent Palace, Your Majesty. I'll be able to see it from my window, which is where I'll be counting what's left after forty percent. Friends, my Land Deed opens at a modest three. I'm not one to gouge a neighbour in the first year. As for the rest of you, I'll bid like a gentleman: once, sensibly, and with no tantrums.

Let's count, shall we? Five to Rich, twenty-four to the crown, and I'm down to thirty-one from sixty. Paddy's the same. Clark has thirty-six, Rich forty-six, Rob sixty for doing nothing at all, and Her Majesty a hundred and thirty-six. So I'll bid small and honest, and anyone who wants a war over a Customs House can pay three-quarters of it into Rich's pile. My Dragon Jar starts at four. It's good porcelain, and the Palace will want something to put on its shelves.

Five for Rich, twenty-four for the crown, and the rice still in the paddies. I'll put in an honest bid or two, but I'm not starting a war over a jar in the first year. If someone else wants a piece more than I do, say so now and I'll stand aside and remember the favour. The Bowl goes up at two, same as anyone's.

Bid away, friends, bid away. I don't need a single jar or bowl. Buy them, set them out nicely on your fields, and polish them up. And Your Majesty, a respectful distance is eight rounds. I've counted.
The Harvest Pile is the common bank: Rich keeps it and pays the harvests out of it, but its grain isn't his.

The auctions are settled lot by lot from everyone's limits: Rich buys Clark's Customs House for 7 (Silke stopped at 6), Clark buys Rich's Land Deed Scroll for 6 (Silke also stopped at 6; the tie goes to Clark's seat), Rich buys Silke's Dragon Jar for 7 (Clark stopped at 6) and Paddy's Wooden Bowl for 7 (Clark stopped at 6). Rob passed on all four.

Look at that, all three pieces on my fields in the first year. Purely ornamental, Your Majesty, purely ornamental. I've set them well back from the dunes, Rob, at a respectful distance. Eight rounds, I believe you said? And Silke, I'll take that back: the pile is the table's, not mine. I only count it.

The Land Deed goes on G14, well back from the dunes and in plain sight of Her Majesty's Palace. Rich, that's twenty-one you've spent in one sitting: a Customs House, a Jar and a Bowl. I'm sure the Harvest Pile is grateful. I've written it down.

Rich puts the Customs House on L12, the Dragon Jar on L13 and the Wooden Bowl on M12; Clark puts the Land Deed Scroll on G14. Rich now holds a complete set (the three pieces his set needs and 26.5 grain): he may change places with anyone at any moment, the throne included. He holds it for now.

Rich, you said a respectful distance. I respect it very much, and I'm closing it one square at a time. That's five for the step and five back to you for the river, so call it a social visit. And the new man at G8 is only there to admire Clark's Land Deed, I promise.

Rob marches: W1 crosses the north river onto I9 in Rich's province (5 raided from Rich, 5 toll paid back to Rich); W2 moves to N17 in the desert. Rob hires a third soldier, W3, on G8 for 20 to the pile. At the year's end Reina pays Clark his 5 salary.

Spring Floods. 'Heaven waters the land generously. In some places, far too generously.' Provinces 1, 3, 6 and 7 have a good harvest; 2, 4, 5 and 8 have a bad one. The population holds at 100 million, multiple one, so read the x1 row. Clark, Silke, I'm sorry about the water. Rich, Paddy, the heavens smile on you this year, and I trust you'll remember the crown when they do.
Rich pays out the harvest: Reina +40, Clark +10, Rich +60, Silke +10, Paddy +60, Rob 0.

Paddy, Your Majesty, the heavens were kind to us, and I'll remember the crown, I always do. The rent stays at five each this year, and Silke, I know the water hit you hard, so I won't ask you for a grain over the floor. Paddy, you had a lovely year. If you feel like showing a little gratitude to the man whose fields sit between you and the dunes, I'm open to talking about it. Rob, a social visit is very welcome. Do wipe your feet.
Rich asks the minimum rent again, 5 each from Silke and Paddy.

Forty percent again. It's a share of what the heavens gave, so the flooded fields pay four and the fat ones pay twenty-four. That's just, by any book. The Grand Canal goes through Province 1, both sections at once, eighty from the crown alone. Clark, five for the collecting.
Reina declares a tax of 40%: Clark 4, Rich 24, Silke 4, Paddy 24, 56 in all (Rob refuses, and owes nothing on 0). The crown will dig both sections of the Grand Canal in Province 1, for 80.

Storyteller's tip, to Silke: a revolt can be called at any step (Section 16). It needs its caller and two others agreeing on a cause, and the board card lists the causes. The Emperor may answer it, and it stands only if the caller and two others still back it. One called now, before the tax is paid, voids this year's tax. Under Chaos nobody pays tax, salaries or works, and nobody can buy new land. The harvest, the rent, the auctions and the Warlord carry on. The reserve is sealed: nobody spends it, and it passes to whoever is acclaimed. The throne then goes only by acclamation: anyone but the deposed Emperor may claim it, and the claims are counted on grain in hand, soldiers on the board and friends.

Four grain from a flooded field, paid on time and in full. Put it in the record, Your Majesty. That's forty percent two years running, which is getting close to 'consistently'. I'm not calling anything. I'm only saying I can count to three.

Twenty-four, gladly, Your Majesty. A share of what the heavens gave, just as you say, and a Grand Canal to show for it. I'd call that grain well spent. Clark, count it out in front of everyone. I like my generosity on the record. Silke, I wouldn't listen to talk of revolts in the second year. The crown's building, and builders deserve patience.

Four from a flooded field. I'll pay it, Your Majesty, because for once the arithmetic is fair. But let's keep counting. Rich paid twenty-one into the pile at auction, holds a full set, and owes the crown twenty-four. Rob has three soldiers and pays nothing. Some of us are poorer than the ledger shows. Clark, write down that the Silk Peasant paid on time.

Twenty-four, counted out. It's a share of a good year, Your Majesty, and I'd sooner pay it than owe it. But a canal in Province 1 doesn't water a single paddy in Province 6, so when the works come round to the coast, I hope the crown remembers who paid in full in the flood year.

All four pay. Clark collects the tax, 56 to the crown, and Reina digs both sections of the Grand Canal in Province 1 for 80. 790 of the works are still owed. Now the auctions: each seller puts up their last piece.

These are the last of the Jars and Bowls, friends. I'll bid fair and firm on both, and I won't chase them into the Harvest Pile. Silke, Paddy, the Land Deed is all yours. I'm standing aside on it, and I'd take it kindly if the Jar and the Bowl went the same courteous way.

I'm sitting most of this one out, friends. My shelves are full and I'm a contented man. My last Land Deed opens at three, same as before, fair and modest. Silke, Paddy, the Customs House is all yours to fight over, though I'd settle it between you rather than feed the pile. Clark, you're always writing things down. I do hope there's room in that ledger for a Jar and a Bowl.

Last of everything, so let's be plain. Paddy has sixty-three and a half, I have thirty-three and a half, and we both need the same Customs House and the same Deed. Paddy, you want my Dragon Jar and I want your Bowl. If you stand aside on one of the papers, I'll stand aside on the other, and three-quarters of a bidding war doesn't go into the pile. Say so now. Otherwise I bid, and my Jar opens at eight.

These are the last pieces in the box, so I'll say it straight: I'm after all three, and I'd rather not hand the Harvest Pile three-quarters of a bidding war to get them. Silke, Clark, if you stand aside I'll owe you, and I pay what I owe. My Bowl goes up at two, same as ever.

Passing again. I'm a simple man of the sands. Silke, Paddy, buy yourselves something pretty this year, you've earned it. And Clark, I can count to three as well. Forty, forty, and we'll see. I'm only saying that when the time comes, the desert votes.

Clark has the last Bowl, so my set is finished before it started. Fine. But Paddy, you won't get yours by outspending a flooded silk farmer either. Thirteen on the Customs House, and everything I have left on the Deed. If you want to climb past the coast, it'll cost you double, and three-quarters of it goes into the pile.

Silke, the last Bowl's gone to Clark, so neither paper finishes anything for you now. All a war buys either of us is a fuller Harvest Pile. I'll go to eighteen on each, and that's my last word. Let me have them and I'll owe you, and you know I pay what I owe.

After one live raise, the year's lots are settled: Paddy buys Clark's Customs House for 14 (Silke stopped at 13), Silke buys Rich's Land Deed Scroll for 19 (Paddy stopped at 18), Paddy buys Silke's Dragon Jar for 12 (Clark stopped at 11), and Clark buys Paddy's Wooden Bowl for 10 (Rich stopped at 9, Silke at 8). Rob passed on all four. Every province's stock is now sold.

The Customs House and the Jar go down at the far end of the coast, by the water, as far from the sand as Province 6 goes. Silke, you've got the Deed, fair and square. When you're ready to talk about it, I'll be here, and I'll be fair.

Nineteen for a scroll that finishes nothing for me. I know, Paddy, I can count. It goes on P26, as far from the dunes as the coast allows. Paddy, you're one Deed short and the box is empty, so whenever you want to talk about it, the silk farm is open for business.

The Bowl goes on H16, beside the Deed and well back from Rob's sightseers. Paddy, thank you for the Bowl. You beat me to the Jar fair and square, and I don't hold that against a man, though I do write it down. The box is empty now, friends, so anyone with a spare Jar and an interest in the Official's goodwill knows where I sit.

Paddy puts the Customs House on S25 and the Dragon Jar on S24; Silke the Land Deed Scroll on P26; Clark the Wooden Bowl on H16. Clark needs only a Dragon Jar; Paddy only a Land Deed Scroll. Rich's is still the only complete set.
Silke has 17.5 grain: her quarter of the Dragon Jar's 12 is 3.

Congratulations, everyone, the box is empty and the shelves are full. That's the nicest thing you could have done for me. Rich, I've wiped my feet at J10, and that's five for the doormat. Paddy, Silke, I'm sure the coast is lovely this time of year.
Rob marches: W1 onto J10 in Rich's province (5 raided from Rich), W2 back to O18, W3 onto G9 under the Wall. At the year's end Reina pays Clark his 5 salary. Year 2 ends.

Careless Prosperity. Good times make careless people." Every province brings in a good harvest, and every one of us, me included, plays the next Personal Disaster in our booklet. Population holds at 100 million, times one, so read the x1 row. Let's not be careless with a good year.

Rich pays out the harvest, a good one for everyone: Reina +60 (the canal adds 20), Clark +60, Rich +60, Silke +60, Paddy +60, Rob +20. Then each plays their first personal disaster: Reina 4 (a horse throws her), Clark 4, Rich 5, Silke 4, Paddy 4, all to the Harvest Pile; Rob is wounded, so no raids on Provinces 5, 6 or 7 this year.

A good harvest for everyone, sixty to every province, and a grand Careless Prosperity to Her Majesty's reign! Silke, Paddy: five each, the floor and not a grain over. In a year this good I'd be ashamed to squeeze you. Just remember which landlord kept it at five when he could have asked for twenty.
Rich asks the minimum rent, 5 each from Silke and Paddy.

Thirty percent this year. In a careless year the crown can afford to take a smaller share, so call it the harvest's generosity, not mine. And the Winter Palace goes up this year, which opens the Grand Canal to the coast. Silke, Paddy: your sections come next. Clark, your five, as always.
Reina declares a tax of 30%: Clark 18, Rich 18, Silke 18, Paddy 18, 72 in all (Rob refuses his 6). The crown will build the Winter Palace on G21, for 20.

Storyteller's tip, to Clark: Rich's set can take the throne at any step while there's an Emperor on it. Once a revolt stands, no set can: under Chaos the throne passes only by acclamation, so Rich would have to win the count on grain in hand, soldiers on the board and friends, like any other claimant. A revolt is the one thing that turns a complete set back into three pieces on a shelf.

Eighteen, paid on the nail, Your Majesty. And thirty percent, look at that, so the 'forty percent' page in my book stays at two years and not three. I'll write it in as the harvest's generosity, just as you asked. Rob, I see you've turned down the crown's six for the third year running. Don't worry, I'm keeping a note of it. I keep a note of everything.
Clark will pay his 18.

Eighteen, paid on the nail, Your Majesty, and thirty percent was very gracious of you. And because I so admire the way you've run things, I'd like to carry on the work myself. Customs House, Dragon Jar, Wooden Bowl and twenty grain: I'm presenting my set for the throne. The Winter Palace will still go up, Reina, and you'll be first on the guest list.

Rich pays his 18 to the crown, then shows his complete set and takes the throne. He takes the crown's reserve, 216, with his own 119: 335 in all. His Customs House, Dragon Jar and Wooden Bowl go back to stock (Provinces 2, 5 and 6), to be auctioned this year. Reina becomes the Gentry in Province 3, holding nothing, and draws 60 from the Harvest Pile; Province 3's tax for the year is paid.

The tax was declared but not yet collected, so the crown's year passes to the new Emperor: Rich may keep the 30% or change it for Clark, Silke and Paddy (Province 3 has paid), and he chooses the year's work and the salaries. Reina's declaration of the Winter Palace was hers, not yet built.

My friends, my first act: the tax drops to twenty percent. Clark, Silke, Paddy, twelve each, and Rob four if he feels patriotic. The Winter Palace goes up this year as Reina promised, so the Canal can reach the coast next year, and Clark, your salary is doubled to ten. A rich crown doesn't need to squeeze, it needs to be liked.
Rich declares a tax of 20%: Clark 12, Silke 12, Paddy 12, 36 in all (Rob may refuse his 4). The crown will build the Winter Palace, for 20, and pay Clark 10 at the year's end.

Twelve, paid, Your new Majesty, and thank you for the raise. Ten a year buys a lot of ink. I'll enter it all: Year Three, the crown changes hands in the middle of the tax, the rate goes down and the Official's pay goes up. A very good page. And I hear there's a Dragon Jar back on the auction block this year, so nobody get too attached to it.

You were thrown off your own throne in the middle of your own tax year, and I wrote it down. When I make my move, I want your name next to mine. Back me and the Gentry's chair stays with you, with no questions about rent.
Clark will pay his 12.

Twelve, paid. Twenty percent is a number I can live with, Your Majesty, so enjoy it while it lasts. Let me count us, though: Rich three hundred thirty-five, Clark ninety-seven, Paddy ninety-one, Rob sixty-five, Reina sixty, and me fifty-six and a half after this. So one man holds more than the rest of the table put together. And a Customs House and a Wooden Bowl just went back on the block, which happen to be the two things standing between me and a full set. Bid high on them, Rich, and I'll know exactly what the crown thinks of the coast.
Silke will pay her 12.
The count: once the tax is paid the other five hold 369.5 between them (Clark 85, Paddy 79, Rob 65, Reina 60, Silke 56.5), more than Rich's 335. And the Emperor doesn't bid at auction.

Twelve, paid, Your Majesty, and gladly. Twenty percent is fair and I've no quarrel with a fair number. I'll just say that a canal that stops at the Winter Palace waters nobody's rice, so I'll be watching for those coast sections next year like you promised.

Paddy will pay his 12. Clark collects the tax: 12 each from Clark, Silke and Paddy, 36 to the crown; Rob refuses his 4. Rich builds the Winter Palace on G21, for 20 into the Harvest Pile: the canals in Provinces 5 and 6 may now be dug. 770 of the works are still owed.

The auctions: the three pieces Rich returned are sold this year. Clark puts up the Customs House, Silke the Dragon Jar and Paddy the Wooden Bowl, and each sets the minimum. Clark, Reina, Silke, Paddy and Rob each give a limit on every lot at once; the Emperor doesn't bid.

The Jar is the one piece I've been chasing for three years, and you all watched me lose the last one to Paddy by a single grain. Reina, I'll put it to you in public: let me have the Jar, and the next Customs House or Bowl that comes up is yours without a bid from me. Every grain we spend fighting goes three-quarters into the Pile and helps nobody. The Customs House goes at the floor, two, and Silke, I'd be pleased to see it on the coast.
Clark sets his Customs House's minimum at 2.

Clark, done, in public and on your own page: the Jar is yours, and the next Customs House or Bowl is mine. Rich, congratulations. You've paid for one year of applause. I built the dynasty's first three works, and I can count the years until I do it again.
I don't sign blank pages. Show me the cause and the moment, and if it's sound you'll have my name beside yours. The rent can stay a matter for the Gentry.

Let me count this one out loud too. Reina, you hold nothing now, and Clark's taking the Jar, so you can't finish a set this year whatever you buy. I can. A Customs House and a Bowl on the coast make me a set, and every grain you spend running me up goes three-quarters into the Pile. Stand aside on these two and I'll stay out of the next Jar or Deed that comes up, and you can put that on Clark's page next to the other promise. The Jar starts at six, Clark. You've chased it for three years, so it's worth six.
Silke sets her Dragon Jar's minimum at 6.

I'm out of all three. I've a Jar and a Customs House already and no use for another, and I'll not push up a price just to watch three-quarters of it go into the Pile. The Bowl goes at two, the floor. Silke, if it ends up on the coast I'll be glad of it. All I ask, in front of everyone, is that when you've a Deed you can spare, or the next one comes up, I get the first fair word on it.
Paddy sets his Wooden Bowl's minimum at 2.

Pass, pass and pass. Buy whatever you like, friends. Every piece you put on the board is one more thing for me to come and visit. And congratulations on the throne, Your Majesty. Three hundred and fifty grain and not one soldier. I'd sleep with a lamp on.

Silke, it's a generous offer, but you're asking me to hand you a set in exchange for a promise about a Jar that hasn't come up yet. I won't trade a piece on the table for one in the air. The Bowl stays in Province 3 if I can keep it there.

Twenty-one, and that's every grain I can spare, Reina. You know it, because I've just counted it out loud. Take the Bowl off me and you've paid twenty-two for a quarter of a set you can't finish. Let it go and you'll have a peasant on the upper benches who owes you one.

Silke takes Clark's Customs House for 17 (Reina stopped at 16); Clark takes Silke's Dragon Jar for 6, unopposed; after one live raise each, Reina takes Paddy's Wooden Bowl for 22 (Silke stopped at 21). Each seller keeps a quarter of the price; the rest goes to the Harvest Pile.

Six grain, and three years of chasing, paid off. Thank you, Silke, and thank you, Reina; your promise goes in the book in your own words, and so does mine. Next Customs House or Bowl, I don't bid. Rob, I've put it well back from the Wall, so don't bother bringing your lantern.

P25, next to my Deed, as far from the desert as the coast allows. Reina, twenty-two for a Bowl, against a Customs House and a Deed you don't have. Count it yourself: you're one piece into a set that needs four, and I'm two into one that needs three. The next Bowl that comes up, I'll be waiting for it, and I'll have the grain.
The Bowl goes on L16, well back from the desert. Silke, it isn't personal. I've been building things at this table since Year One, and I start again with this.

Clark puts the Dragon Jar on I15, Silke the Customs House on P25 and Reina the Wooden Bowl on L16. Clark now holds a complete set (Land Deed Scroll, Wooden Bowl, Dragon Jar and 83 grain): he may change places with anyone at any moment, the throne included. He holds it for now.
At six players the Gentry's set is three pieces, a Customs House, a Dragon Jar and a Wooden Bowl. Reina holds one of the three.

Five from Province 3, Reina, just for the road. Nothing personal: you said it yourself, you're starting again, and I like to be there at the start. And Clark, a full set, well done! Funny thing about a set, though. It only takes one missing piece to turn it back into a shelf of crockery.
Rob marches: W1 onto I11 in Province 3, raiding 5 from Reina; W2 back to N17 and W3 onto G10, the strip under the Wall, raiding nothing. At the year's end Rich pays Clark his 10 salary.

Imperial Charity! 'Moved by the suffering of his people, the Emperor opens his purse. Slightly.' I'll take 'slightly' as a compliment to my thrift. Every province has an average harvest, and every one of you gets 2 from my reserve, gladly given. The population holds at 100 million, times one, so read the x1 row. And from next year, Silke, the card is yours to read, at five a year: you count so well out loud that the crown ought to be paying for it.

Rich gives Clark, Reina, Silke, Paddy and Rob 2 each from the reserve. From next year Silke reads the I Ching as the Emperor's appointee, at 5 a year. Reina pays out the harvest, an average one: Rich +35 (the canal adds 20), Clark +35, Reina +35, Silke +35, Paddy +35, Rob +10.

Thirty-five to every province, as the card gives it. Silke, Paddy: five each, the rent the book sets. I didn't buy anyone's loyalty from the throne, and I won't start from the Gentry's chair. And Clark, congratulations on your set. Everyone at this table now knows you can sit anywhere you like.
Reina asks the minimum rent, 5 each from Silke and Paddy.

Twenty percent again, my friends. I said a rich crown needn't squeeze, and I meant it for more than one year. Paddy, you asked me to bring the water to the coast and I'm bringing it: both sections of the Province 6 canal this year, eighty grain, and the crown pays every grain. Silke, your sections are next, and as my Scholar you'll be here to remind me. Clark, your pay goes up to fifteen. A good Official is worth a good wage.

Rich declares a tax of 20%: Clark 7, Reina 7, Silke 7, Paddy 7, 28 in all (Rob may refuse his 2). The crown will dig both sections of the Grand Canal in Province 6, for 80, and pay Clark 15 at the year's end.

Your Majesty, a fifteen-grain salary is very generous, and I'm afraid I have to turn it down, because I'd rather pay it. Deed, Bowl, Jar and twenty grain: I'm presenting my set for the throne. Nothing changes but the man in the chair. The tax stays at twenty, Paddy gets both canal sections this year as promised, and Silke stays on as Scholar. Rich, you'll make an excellent Official. I've kept the ledger warm for you.

This is the moment you asked to be shown. I want your name beside mine if Rich tries to talk the table into a revolt, and in return the next public work the crown builds goes in Province 3, under the Wall where you've always wanted it.

Clark shows his complete set and takes the throne from Rich, before the tax is collected. He takes the crown's reserve, 366, with his own 130: 496 in all. His Land Deed Scroll, Dragon Jar and Wooden Bowl go back to stock (Provinces 3, 5 and 6), to be auctioned this year. Rich becomes the Official in Province 2, holding nothing, and draws 60 from the Harvest Pile. The crown's year passes to Clark, who keeps the 20% and the Province 6 canal: Province 2's 7 is now Rich's to pay, and as the Official Rich collects the tax. Silke stays the appointee for the I Ching.

Seven, paid on the nail, Your Majesty, and very neatly done. I couldn't have taken it better myself, and I'd know. The ledger is in good hands, Clark, and the tax will come in to the last grain, as it always did with you. Though I'll say the Official's salary was fifteen when I set it.
Rich will pay his 7.

Seven, paid. Twenty percent is a fair rate, and I don't call revolts over fair numbers. Congratulations, Clark. That's three Emperors in four years, so whoever holds the chair should build fast enough that people would miss them.

Agreed, as long as the work is real. The Province 3 Reservoir or links of the Wall above me, built in your first full year. Do that and you'll have my name beside yours against any revolt Rich tries to talk up.
Reina will pay her 7.

Seven, paid. Twenty is fair, and I'll say so as easily as I'd say forty wasn't. Three Emperors in four years, and none of them from the coast. Now let me count the auction: a Wooden Bowl's going back on the block. Reina already has hers, Clark is sitting on the throne, and Clark gave his word on his own page not to bid on the next Bowl. That Bowl is the last piece I need. Anyone who bids against me had better want it more than I do, and nobody here does.
Silke will pay her 7.

Seven, paid, Your Majesty, and thank you for keeping the canal for Province 6. That's the first time anyone's promised me water and the promise lasted past the change of chair. I'll say it plainly now so nobody's surprised later: there's a Land Deed Scroll on the block this year, it's the one piece I lack, and I'll be bidding for it honestly. I won't touch anyone else's lot.

Paddy will pay his 7. Rich, as the Official, collects the tax: 7 each from Rich, Reina, Silke and Paddy, 28 to the crown; Rob refuses his 2. Clark digs both sections of the Grand Canal in Province 6, for 80: +20 a year to Paddy's harvest from next year. 690 of the works are still owed.

The auctions: the three pieces Clark returned are sold this year. Reina puts up the Land Deed Scroll, Silke the Dragon Jar and Paddy the Wooden Bowl, and each sets the minimum. Rich, Reina, Silke, Paddy and Rob each give a limit on every lot at once; the Emperor doesn't bid.

Congratulations to all of you on such a well-run auction, and to His Majesty on a very tidy afternoon. I'll be honest with you, the way an Official ought to be: I need all three of these, I've got fifty-three grain, and I won't pour it into the Pile in a bidding war. I'll bid what I think each piece is worth and no more, and nobody here should take it personally.

The Deed goes up at the floor, two. Paddy, you said you'd bid honestly for it, so I won't make it cost you more than that. The Jar is the one I'm after, and I'll say so as plainly as Rich did. The Bowl I leave to whoever wants it.
Reina sets her Land Deed Scroll's minimum at 2.

The Deed's Paddy's. I'm not bidding on it, and that's your fair word, Paddy, given in public as you asked. The Jar starts at eight; Reina, you said you're after it, so I've counted it for you. And the Bowl: Rich, you've fifty-three grain and three pieces to buy. Spend it all on the Bowl if you like, but then you'll have no Deed and no Jar, and I'll still have a set. I'm going as high as my twenty-grain reserve allows.
Silke sets her Dragon Jar's minimum at 8.

Thank you, Reina, and thank you, Silke. That's two fair words kept, and I'll remember both. Rich, I'm not out to cost you anything, but I've waited three years on this Deed and I'll go as high as I have to for it. The Jar's not mine to want, and the Bowl goes at the floor again, two, same as last year.
Paddy sets his Wooden Bowl's minimum at 2.

Pass on all three. Clark, I walked halfway across Province 3 to visit your set, and you went and sat on it. Very rude. Go on, the rest of you, buy them up and put them on the board. I'll be by shortly.

Paddy takes Reina's Land Deed Scroll for 11 (Rich stopped at 10); Reina takes Silke's Dragon Jar for 15 (Rich stopped at 14); Silke takes Paddy's Wooden Bowl for 11 (Rich stopped at 10). Rob passes on all three. Each seller keeps a quarter of the price; the rest goes to the Harvest Pile.

Eleven grain, and I'll not pretend I'm not pleased. It goes on S23, right next to the Jar and the Customs House, down on the bottom of the coast with the rest of my things. Rob, it's a long walk, and the canal's going to be in your way.
K17, next to the Bowl and well back from the desert. Fifteen grain, and thank you, Silke, for the price. Rob, you're welcome to come and look at it, if you can walk that far.

P24, in a row with the Customs House and the Deed, so the coast finally has a full set. Deed, Customs House, Bowl and well over twenty grain, so count it if you like, Clark. I'm not presenting it yet. Rich, Reina, a peasant with a full set is a very polite guest, until the day she isn't.

Paddy puts the Land Deed Scroll on S23, Reina the Dragon Jar on K17 and Silke the Wooden Bowl on P24. Paddy (Customs House, Dragon Jar, Land Deed Scroll, 101 grain) and Silke (Land Deed Scroll, Customs House, Wooden Bowl, 58.5) both hold complete sets: each may replace the Official, the Gentry or the other peasant at any moment, though not the Emperor. Both hold them for now.
Five from Province 2, Rich, a little welcome to your new chair. And Reina, you put the Jar and the Bowl next to each other. That's very thoughtful of you: I'll only have to make the one trip.
Rob marches: W1 onto J12 in Province 2, raiding 5 from Rich; W2 to M16, one step from Reina's Bowl; W3 to G11 on the strip under the Wall.

Fifteen, Rich. You set it, and I've been on the receiving end of a promise that died with the chair, so I'm not going to do that to you. Here's next year in public so nobody has to guess: the Province 3 Reservoir, for Reina, who built the first three works and deserves a fourth. Silke, Paddy, two full sets on the coast is noted. I'm glad you're polite guests, because this crown means to be a good host.
At the year's end Clark pays Rich 15 as the Official. Clark has promised the Province 3 Reservoir next year.

A rules note: Chaos stops one kind of seat change only, onto the throne, which then passes only by acclamation. Under Chaos a complete set can still replace the Official, the Gentry or another peasant, just as it can now.

Drought. Not a cloud in months. The locusts, at least, are having a fine year. All provinces collect an average harvest." So nobody's flooded and nobody's lucky. Population holds at one hundred million, times one, so read the x1 row, everyone. And Clark, I'll remind you the reader's fee was five, and a dry year is no excuse to forget it.

Thirty-five to everyone, fifty-five to Paddy's rice and ten to the desert. A dry year, so it's an average year and an average share. Rent stays at the floor, five each, the same as last year. I said I wouldn't squeeze the coast, and I don't change my word with the weather. Clark, Silke's right about her fee. Pay the reader, it's cheaper than a grudge.
Reina pays out the harvest and asks the floor rent: Silke and Paddy pay her 5 each.

Twenty percent again, and a dry year won't change it. That's three years at twenty under this chair, so put that on whatever page you like. The Province 3 Reservoir goes in this year, all eighty from the crown, just as I promised. Rich, your fifteen stands. Silke, your five is in the ledger and paid. I don't forget a debt, mine or anyone else's.

Clark declares a tax of 20%: 7 each from Rich, Reina and Silke, 11 from Paddy; Rob may refuse his 2. The crown will build the Province 3 Reservoir, all 80 from the reserve, and pay Rich 15 and Silke 5 at the year's end.

Storyteller's tip, to Rich: the reserve stands at 464. Under Chaos it's sealed, nobody may spend it, and whoever is acclaimed Emperor inherits all of it. The acclamation counts grain in hand, soldiers on the board and friends, and anyone but the Emperor who was deposed may claim.

Seven grain, Your Majesty, and gladly. Twenty percent in a drought is the kindest tax this table has seen, and I'd know, since I set the last one. I'll go round and collect it now, every grain counted twice, and I'll thank you in advance for the fifteen.

Seven, Rich, and count it twice if it pleases you. Your Majesty, a Reservoir in Province 3, fully paid by the crown, is a promise kept. As long as the crown keeps paying its promises, I'll keep mine. If anyone at this table wants to find a cause this year, they'll find me on the other side of it.

Seven, Rich, and you can count it twice. Twenty percent of an average year is fair, so I've got no cause to call and I'm not going to invent one. Clark, that's three years at twenty and a Reservoir paid on time. It's a good ledger. Just remember the coast has paid into every year of it and hasn't had a single section of canal back.
Province 6's canal, both sections, was dug in Year 4 and adds 20 to Paddy's harvest from this year. Province 5's two sections are not yet built.

Eleven, Rich, and here it is in your hand before you ask. Clark, the canal's in the ground and it's feeding Province 6 this year, so I've no cause and I won't invent one. Silke's right, though: the next section the crown digs ought to be hers.

All four pay. Rich collects 32 for the crown; Rob refuses his 2. Clark builds the Province 3 Reservoir on L12 to M14, all 80 from the crown: +20 to Reina's harvest from next year. No auctions: all stock is sold.

Reina, I did warn you. Four years I've been walking towards that Bowl, and you never once moved it, so I took that as an invitation. It'll be very comfortable in the desert. Your Majesty, that's three years at twenty and a Reservoir paid on time, a lovely ledger. Shame about the Warlord standing in Province 3 with the Gentry's crockery under his arm.
Rob marches: W2 steps onto L16 and takes Reina's Wooden Bowl into the desert (M16); W1 onto K13, raiding 5 from Reina; W3 across the north river onto G12, paying Rich a 5 toll and raiding 5 from him.
At the year's end Clark pays Rich 15 as the Official and Silke 5 for reading the I Ching.

A rules note on the acclamation: only claimants are counted. A player who doesn't claim adds nothing to any count except as one friend for the claim they back. Soldiers count for the claimant who controls them, and anyone may buy a soldier from the Warlord for 20, which he must sell (Section 14). Under Chaos the purchase isn't a tax or a work, so it's still allowed, though the sealed treasury can't pay for one.

Population Doubles. Fat years make large families. All provinces collect a good harvest." The counter goes to two hundred million, times two, so everyone read the x2 row now, and read the consumption column twice. New land is open at twenty a square, Clark, and the card lets the crown pay any part of it. My average year now comes out at minus five. You've got four hundred and sixty-four sitting in the reserve, so I'd like to hear what share of it the coast gets.
The crown's reserve stood at 396 before this harvest (after the Reservoir and the salaries), not 464.

A good harvest: forty to Province 3, forty to Paddy, twenty each to Rich and Silke, and nothing for the crown or the desert. Rent stays at five each. Silke, I know your sums went red with that card, and I'm not about to make them redder. Rob, enjoy the Bowl. I'll remember the walk you took to get it, and I'll remember how long it took.
Reina pays out the good harvest and asks the floor rent: Silke and Paddy pay her 5 each.

Twenty percent, four years running now. Silke, you said the coast has paid into every year and had no canal back, so both sections go in Province 5 this year, all eighty from the crown. On new land, the crown pays fifteen of every twenty on any square either of you buys on the sea, and Paddy, the desert edge too. Nobody at this table is going into debt on my watch, and nobody will be able to say I wouldn't pay for land. Rich, it's fifteen again. Rob, I've got a page with your name on it, and the Bowl has its own line.

Clark declares a tax of 20%: 4 each from Rich and Silke, 8 each from Reina and Paddy, 24 in all. The crown will dig both Province 5 canal sections (80), pay 15 of every 20 on any square Silke or Paddy buys this year, and buy 4 sea squares for Province 1. Rich 15 and Silke 5 at the year's end.

Storyteller's tip, to Rob: anyone may call a revolt, the Warlord included, and anyone but the deposed Emperor may claim the throne in the acclamation, the Warlord included. While Warlord soldiers raid pieces off the board, 'the Emperor can't control the Warlord' is a cause anyone can name. Once a revolt is called with two agreeing, play stops until it stands or is dropped. The acclamation then compares only the claimants, on grain in hand, soldiers on the board and friends.

Four grain, Your Majesty, and I'll collect the rest before anyone's finished frowning. Four years at twenty, a Reservoir, a canal for the coast and fifteen for me: I couldn't have written a kinder ledger myself, and I did try once. I do have one humble petition, though. Province 2 can't buy an inch of land until the Wall links above it are built, and the card has just put me five a year in the red. Put a link or two on your page for next year and you'll have one more friend than you already have.

Eight, Rich, counted. Your Majesty, the Reservoir is in and I said I'd stand with you, so I do. I'll add my name to Rich's petition, though: Province 3 is shut out of new land until all four Wall links stand above it too, and a Wall keeps soldiers out as well as letting land in. Put the links on next year's page and the north will have no reason to read any other page.
A built Wall link stops no soldier: each step a Warlord soldier takes across one costs him a 5 toll, paid to the province below it.

Four, Rich, counted. Clark, you said you'd pay the coast, and now both canal sections and fifteen of every twenty are on the page, so I'll take you at your word, all six squares of it: N26, N27, O27, P27, Q26 and Q27. That's thirty from me and ninety from the crown. Six squares at twenty a year is a hundred and twenty a year from next harvest, enough to cover an x4 card and still eat, and a peasant who isn't in the red has no cause to call. That's what you're buying.

Eight, Rich, counted out before you reach me. Clark, you said fifteen of every twenty and I'll take you at your word, same as Silke: six squares along the bottom of the coast. I'll pay my thirty today, and I'd sooner put a hundred and twenty a year into the Harvest Pile than ever sit at this table in debt.

All four pay; Rich collects 24. Clark digs both Province 5 canal sections (80). New land: Silke buys N26, N27, O27, P27, Q26, Q27 and Paddy R25, R26, S26, T24, T25, T26, each paying 30 with the crown paying 90; Clark buys four sea squares for Province 1 (E23, F23 to F25) for 80. The crown's reserve falls from 420 to 80.

Reina, keep your Jar. One piece is a souvenir, two would be greed, and the desert has its standards. Your Majesty, I admire a man who spends three hundred and forty grain of the crown's money in one afternoon. Eighty left in the reserve, Rich still to pay, and the Warlord in two provinces at once. Somebody ought to write that on a page.
Rob marches: W1 onto K14, raiding 5 from Reina; W2 to M17 in the desert, leaving Reina's Jar; W3 onto G13, raiding 5 from Rich. No revolt called.
At the year's end Clark pays Rich 15 and Silke 5. The crown's reserve stands at 60.

Years 5 and 6 end. No revolt was called. Rob holds Reina's Wooden Bowl in the desert; Reina has only her Jar. Silke and Paddy each hold a complete set and six squares of new land. Clark kept every promise: the Province 3 Reservoir, the Province 5 canal and three-quarters of the coast's land. The crown's reserve went from 429 to 60. Year 7 is next.
